entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:3, the Servant was despised and rejected by people.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Observe how the people treated the Servant.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: The text says he was despised and the most rejected; no one paid him any attention.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of Isaiah 53:3: he was despised and considered the most rejected.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Look at the start of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:6, tap who laid on the Servant the iniquity of us all.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Identify who places the people's guilt on the Servant.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: The one acting at the end of the verse is God: he lays the guilt of all on the Servant.

feedbackWrong.b: "Cada um" (each one) turned to their own way; someone else acts upon the Servant.
feedbackWrong.c: "Todos nós" (all of us) are the ones who went astray, not the one who laid the guilt.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Look for who acts after the "mas".

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.question: According to Isaiah 53:6, how were all of us living?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Observe the image Isaiah uses for the people.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: The text compares everyone to sheep gone astray, each one on its own way.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says the opposite: each one turned to their own way.
feedbackWrong.c: There was no united flock; each one went off in a different direction.
feedbackWrong.d: The verse doesn't speak of fear; it speaks of sheep that got lost.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Read the first sentence of the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.question: Put Isaiah 53:5 in the order of the text.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: That's the verse's sequence: his wound, the punishment on him, and the healing for us.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the pierced Servant; the people's healing closes the verse.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: The verse ends with what happens to the people.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:7, how was the Servant led to the slaughter?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Remember the image Isaiah uses for the Servant's silence.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: Like a lamb, he goes to the slaughter without resisting and without opening his mouth.

feedbackWrong.a: "Bezerro" (calf) doesn't fit: the text doesn't speak of cattle; the image comes from a flock of sheep.
feedbackWrong.b: Close: "carneiro" is a ram; the text uses the youngest, gentlest animal of the flock.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: The image comes from the same flock as the sheep in verse 6.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.question: What does Isaiah 53:5 communicate that connects to this context?
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Connect Isaiah 53:5 to the idea that the Servant suffers for others.
entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: The transgressions are "nossas" (ours): the Servant suffers for what the people did.

feedbackWrong.a: There is a reason, and the text states it: the people's transgressions.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says "nossas transgressões" (our transgressions), not his.

entender-a-biblia-sem-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Look at whose transgressions they are.

options.a: He suffers for no reason at all
options.b: He suffers for his own mistakes
options.c: He suffers in the people's place

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:4–5, the text confirms the people's view that the Servant was punished for his own guilt.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between the people's opinion and the truth about the Servant.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: The "porém" corrects the people: he wasn't paying for his own guilt; he was wounded for ours.

feedbackWrong.true: The people thought so in verse 4, but verse 5 turns the sentence around: he was pierced for our transgressions.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Compare what the people thought with what comes right after.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:4–5, tap the word that corrects what the people thought of the Servant.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Recognize the contrast marker in the text.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: "Porém" turns the page: they thought God was punishing him, but he suffered for us.

feedbackWrong.b: "Feridas" (wounds) shows the suffering, not the correction of what the people thought.
feedbackWrong.c: "Paz" (peace) is the result of the punishment on him, not the word that marks the turn.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Look for a short word between commas at the start of verse 5.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:6, how does the people's straying connect to what the Lord does?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Relate the people's straying to the Lord's action on the Servant.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: The "mas" changes direction: the guilt of those who strayed falls on one alone.

feedbackWrong.b: The text says the iniquity of all fell on him, not on each person.
feedbackWrong.c: The Lord doesn't abandon the people; he lays the people's guilt on the Servant.
feedbackWrong.d: No one comes back on their own in the text; the one who acts is the Lord.

options.a: The people stray, and the guilt of all falls on the Servant
options.b: Each one strays and pays alone for their own guilt
options.c: The people stray, and the Lord leaves them lost
options.d: The people stray and find their own way back

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.question: How does the scene move forward in Isaiah 53:5–6?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: First the Servant's wound, then the picture of the lost people, and finally the guilt on him.

feedbackWrong.default: Verse 5 speaks of the wounded Servant; verse 6 shows the sheep and ends with the guilt on him.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: The passage ends with the Lord's action.

options.a: He is wounded for the people's guilt
options.b: The people get lost like sheep
options.c: The guilt of all falls on him

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:4, what did the Servant do with our pains?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Understand the Servant's action on behalf of the people.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: He took on himself what was ours: the pains pass from the people to the Servant.

feedbackWrong.b: "Ignorou" (ignored) is the opposite: he took our infirmities on himself.
feedbackWrong.c: "Causou" (caused) doesn't fit: the pains were the people's; he took them on himself.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: The verb repeats the idea of "tomou sobre si" (took on himself).

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.question: What connects Isaiah 53:5 to 1 Peter 2:24?
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: See how the New Testament reads Isaiah 53 in light of the cross.
entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: Peter uses Isaiah's words: Jesus bore our sins, and by his wounds we have been healed.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts say he bore the sins of others, not his own.
feedbackWrong.c: Peter ties the healing to sin: having died to sins, we live for righteousness.

entender-a-biblia-cam-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Compare the end of the two verses.

options.c: A healing of the body only

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.question: Isaiah 53:6 presents straying as a problem of the whole people, not just of some.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Interpret the reach of the straying and of the Servant's work.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: "Todos nós" went astray, and it is the iniquity "de todos nós" that falls on him.

feedbackWrong.false: The verse begins and ends with "todos nós" (all of us): no one is left out of the straying.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Notice the words that open and close the verse.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:9, tap the phrase that shows the Servant was not suffering for his own guilt.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Support the Servant's innocence from the text.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: He was innocent: his suffering didn't come from anything he had done.

feedbackWrong.a: "Entre os ímpios" says where they meant to bury him, not how he lived.
feedbackWrong.c: "Com o rico" speaks of his death, not of his innocence.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Look for what the verse says about his conduct.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.question: What reading does Isaiah 53:4–5 support about the Servant's suffering?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about the Servant's suffering.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: He carries what was ours, and the result is peace and healing for the people.

feedbackWrong.a: That's what the people thought, but the "porém" in verse 5 corrects that idea.
feedbackWrong.c: The transgressions are "nossas" (ours); the text never puts the guilt on him.
feedbackWrong.d: The text goes beyond an example: by his wounds we are healed.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Compare what the people thought (v. 4) with what the text states (v. 5).

options.a: His suffering proves God rejected him
options.b: He suffers in the people's place, and that brings healing
options.c: He suffers because he himself had sinned
options.d: He is just an example of patience to imitate

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.question: Which sequence shows the path from Isaiah 53:5 to the proclamation of Jesus?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: See Isaiah 53 as a promise the New Testament sees fulfilled in Jesus.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: The prophet announces, Jesus fulfills it on the cross, and the church reads Isaiah pointing to him.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: prophecy (Isa 53:5), cross (1 Pet 2:24) and proclamation (Acts 8:35).

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Start with the prophet and end with someone who reads the prophet.

options.a: Isaiah sees the Servant wounded for the people's guilt
options.b: Jesus bears our sins in his body on the cross
options.c: Philip reads Isaiah 53 and proclaims Jesus

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.question: In Isaiah 53:6, what did the Lord lay on the Servant?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the meaning of the scene.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: It's the piled-up guilt of all, laid on one: the heart of the Servant's work.

feedbackWrong.b: "Doença" (illness) recalls verse 4; here what falls on him is the guilt of all.
feedbackWrong.c: "Vergonha" (shame) doesn't fit: he was despised, but verse 6 speaks of the guilt of all laid on him.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: It's the same idea as "transgressões" (transgressions) in verse 5.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.question: What connects Isaiah 53:7 to John 1:29?
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.learningObjective: Connect Isaiah's Servant to the Lamb announced by John the Baptist.
entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.feedbackCorrect: The Servant goes like a lamb; John the Baptist points to Jesus, the Lamb who takes away sin.

feedbackWrong.a: Both texts speak of a person, not of animals in the temple.
feedbackWrong.c: The Servant wins in silence, like a lamb, not by force.

entender-a-biblia-pro-entrada-biblia-05-.hint: Look for the image that appears in both texts.

options.b: The Lamb who takes away sin
options.c: A king who wins by force

estudo:entrada-biblia-05.context: Centuries before Jesus, the prophet Isaiah speaks of a Servant of the Lord. In this passage, the people look at this wounded, humiliated Servant and try to understand why he suffers so much.
estudo:entrada-biblia-05.focusQuestion: What changes in you when you know someone carried your guilt?
estudo:entrada-biblia-05.keywordGloss: In Isaiah, the Servant of the Lord suffers for the people; the New Testament recognizes Jesus in him.
facts: The Servant was despised and rejected by people.
The Servant was pierced for our transgressions.
By his wounds the people are healed.
Everyone had gone astray like sheep.
The Lord laid on the Servant the iniquity of all.
Oppressed and humiliated, he stayed silent.
